newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets to vote Tuesday on sheep offal ban.
newsitem.headline: EU vets to vote Tuesday on sheep offal ban.

text.p: The European Union's Standing Veterinary Committee will vote on Tuesday on a new Commission proposal to remove suspect tissue from sheep and goat meat as well as beef, a Commission spokesman said on Monday.
"The Commission plans to put it to a vote," he said.
The Commission delayed forcing a vote on Friday after many member states raised objections to the proposal, designed to protect consumers.
The objectors said the measures were economically unjustified as the risk involved was negligible.
Only Britain, France and Ireland previously expressed any support for the proposal, based on advice from the Scientific Veterinary Committee.
Denmark and Portugal have shown partial support.
If there is no qualified majority in support of the proposal it will be sent to the Farm Council on December 16-17.
A previous Commission proposal to remove sheep brains, spleens and spinal cords from human and animal food was rejected by the committee in August.

But the Commission continued to insist that the proposal was a necessary precaution to protect public health after British and French research had shown that BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) could affect sheep.
